claims.text: The labour-slack pre-read puts the unemployment rate exactly at its estimated natural rate, with zero gap, signalling a labour market neither tight nor slack — a neutral, hold-consistent reading.
Three-month average payrolls are running well below the estimated breakeven pace of 75.0k, pointing to a softening hiring trend that leans toward easier policy.
The breakeven payrolls benchmark of 75.0k exceeds the 50.7k three-month average, reinforcing that job creation is undershooting what is needed — a dovish signal.
The Sahm indicator is very low at 0.033, far from any recession-style deterioration, so there is no acute labour-market distress compelling a cut.
Weekly jobless claims remain low at roughly 198k on a four-week basis, indicating few layoffs and an underlying labour market that is not collapsing — a mildly hawkish counterweight to soft payrolls.

The committee's median unemployment projection for 2026 is 4.1 percent, and it was revised down from the prior 4.3 percent, implying expectations of a somewhat stronger-than-before labour market, which leans slightly hawkish.

The latest statement characterises employment as balanced, with hiring matching workforce growth and little change in unemployment — language consistent with holding rather than hiking or cutting on labour grounds.
claims.quote: Job gains have kept pace with the workforce, and the unemployment rate has changed little.

output.summary: The labour-market evidence is close to balanced and argues mainly for a hold, with only a very slight dovish lean. The pre-read shows unemployment exactly at its natural rate (gap_pp: 0.0) and a low Sahm reading (0.033), both neutral. The clearest dovish signal is payrolls running below breakeven (3m avg 50.7k vs breakeven 75.0k), suggesting softening hiring. Offsetting this, jobless claims remain low (~198k) and the committee revised its 2026 unemployment projection down to 4.1 from 4.3, both pointing to an underlying labour market that is holding up. The September statement calls employment balanced ('Job gains have kept pace with the workforce, and the unemployment rate has changed little'). Net tilt: -1bp, a marginal dovish lean within an essentially hold-consistent labour picture.
